# Dotenvx

> Encrypt your .env files, commit the encrypted files with your code, and decrypt them at runtime with a separate private key.

## Start here

Install the CLI. It works with any language or framework:

```bash
curl -sfS 'https://dotenvx.sh' | sh
```

Follow the current Quickstart before changing a project's environment files. It explains key custody, what to commit, and how to configure a separate production key.

- [Install](https://dotenvx.com/docs/install.md): CLI installation, Armor installation, Windows, and SDK options.
- [Quickstart](https://dotenvx.com/docs/quickstart.md): Encrypt, commit, and run your first .env, then configure production.
- [Docs](https://dotenvx.com/docs.md): Current guides, SDKs, CLI commands, custody options, and reference material.
- [Advanced](https://dotenvx.com/docs/advanced.md): Browse configuration and command references.

## Choose the relevant documentation

- [Guides](https://dotenvx.com/docs/guides.md): Languages, frameworks, deployment platforms, CI, and coding agents.
- [SDKs](https://dotenvx.com/docs/sdk.md): Use dotenvx directly from your application.
- [CLI](https://dotenvx.com/docs/cli.md): Command reference.
- [Custody](https://dotenvx.com/docs/custody.md): Choose where private keys live and how they are accessed.
- [Local custody](https://dotenvx.com/docs/custody/local.md): .env.keys and operating-system secret stores.
- [Armor custody](https://dotenvx.com/docs/custody/armor.md): Managed access to private keys.
- [Password managers](https://dotenvx.com/docs/custody/password-managers.md): 1Password and Bitwarden key custody.
- [Dotenvx.toml](https://dotenvx.com/docs/dotenvxtoml.md): Environment-variable declarations, validation, encryption, and redaction rules.
- [Dotenvx.toml Quickstart](https://dotenvx.com/docs/dotenvxtoml/quickstart.md): Set up your first rules file.

## Current documentation and history

Use the current docs for implementation. Check the installed version against the relevant release notes when working with an existing installation. Blog posts describe the product at their publication date and may discuss future plans.

- [Changelog](https://dotenvx.com/changelog.md): Dated product changes and release links.
- [Blog](https://dotenvx.com/blog.md): Articles, tutorials, and development notes.

Page-level Markdown exports are available through each page's markdown link. Links inside those exports may lead to the corresponding HTML documentation.

[Expanded current documentation](https://dotenvx.com/llms-full.txt) combines the current homepage, product pages, and documentation. It is generated from the site's page-level Markdown exports on every build. Blog posts and the historical changelog are linked above rather than included in that implementation reference.
